title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #5

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

14. A — 100 °C
